### Executive Summary
- **Prioritize Puppet and internet-facing Apache:** CISA confirms exploitation of the Puppet flaw; Apache HTTP/2 RCE exploitation is reported. Establish exposure and mitigation owners this shift.
- **Check software and browser supply chains:** reported malicious `agent-framework` releases threaten Azure/GitHub credentials; poisoned web content creates session-theft, payment-skimming and mobile-exploitation risks.
- **Validate the new OpenJDK RCE urgently:** prioritize externally reachable Java services. This briefing uses supplied reporting; affected builds, fixes and secondary-source claims require vendor confirmation.

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1. Puppet Enterprise — exploited management-plane RCE**
- **What happened:** [CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to KEV](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/11/17/cisa-adds-one-known-exploited-vulnerability-catalog); report deserialization permits code execution using a CA-signed agent certificate.
- **Operational impact:** configuration-management compromise could affect many managed systems; weak autosigning could let an unauthenticated attacker obtain the required certificate.
- **Today:** identify Puppet servers and restrict access to approved agents/admin paths; have platform owners validate vendor fixes and disable unverified certificate autosigning.

**2. Apache HTTP Server — reported active exploitation**
- **What happened:** [Reporting identifies CVE-2026-119618](https://cybersecuritynews.com/apache-http-server-rce-exploitation/) as unauthenticated `mod_http2` RCE, reportedly fixed in Apache 2.4.71.
- **Operational impact:** exposed banking sites, APIs and reverse proxies could provide an entry point; exposure depends on affected builds and where HTTP/2 is actually processed.
- **Today:** map externally reachable HTTP/2-enabled Apache instances and validate the advisory; expedite approved fixes or assess disabling HTTP/2 on affected listeners with service owners.

**3. PyPI `agent-framework` — reported credential-stealing releases**
- **What happened:** [Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 reportedly contained malware](https://cybersecuritynews.com/microsofts-agent-framework-pypi-package/) that could execute at normal Python startup without an application importing the package.
- **Operational impact:** developer systems, CI runners and containers may expose Azure identities and GitHub credentials; application import searches alone will miss potentially affected environments.
- **Today:** block those versions and search installation/build records; where installed, isolate affected runners/hosts and initiate credential revocation plus clean rebuilds through incident response.

**4. OpenJDK “Java4Shell” — new RCE disclosure**
- **What happened:** [Tenable reports CVE-2026-114938](https://www.tenable.com/blog/java4shell-cve-2026-114938-frequently-asked-questions-about-openjdk-rce-vulnerability), involving Base64 decoding; Oracle fixes reportedly shipped November 17, while application-specific exploits remain withheld.
- **Operational impact:** exposed Java applications warrant rapid assessment, but application reachability and affected runtime builds matter; the supplied context does not establish active exploitation.
- **Today:** inventory runtime builds behind critical customer-facing services; have application owners validate vendor applicability and schedule emergency runtime updates where affected.

**5. Poisoned web content — skimming, session theft and iOS risk**
- **What happened:** [Censys describes supply-chain poisoning delivering iOS exploits](https://censys.com/blog/mch-and-caishen-supply-chain-poisoning-pushes-ios-exploits/); separate reporting attributes malicious JavaScript on major sites to an Optimizely compromise.
- **Operational impact:** affected third-party scripts could compromise customer-facing payment journeys; staff browsing may expose sessions or devices. Our own vendor exposure remains unconfirmed.
- **Today:** check Optimizely usage and recent third-party script changes with web owners; retrieve validated campaign indicators and hunt historical browser/proxy contacts before applying targeted controls.

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **Puppet — CA, Puppet Server and EDR logs:** correlate unexpected certificate enrollment/autosigning with report submissions, service-account child processes and unusual server egress; escalate correlated execution evidence.
- **Apache — access/error logs, WAF and EDR:** hunt crashes or error spikes followed by web-worker shells, new executable files or outbound connections; generic anomalies are not exploit confirmation.
- **Java — JVM crash logs, application telemetry and EDR:** correlate new runtime failures with suspicious child processes or egress on exposed services; do not alert on Base64 use alone.
- **PyPI — artifact-proxy logs, CI manifests and endpoint package inventories:** search exact malicious version installations, including cached wheels and built images; preserve package provenance and execution timelines.
- **Azure/GitHub — Entra sign-in, service-principal and GitHub audit logs:** investigate new credential use, app credentials, workflow changes and repository access associated with exposed build/developer identities.
- **Web poisoning — DNS, secure-web-gateway and browser telemetry:** match validated campaign indicators and correlate affected browsing with suspicious downloads or sessions; Censys-sinkholed destinations do not necessarily indicate live attacker control.
- **Customer web — script-integrity/CSP telemetry and deployment logs:** investigate unapproved script changes and unexpected outbound destinations on login/payment pages; prioritize changes outside authorized releases.

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Runtime assurance:** reconcile Java and Apache inventories across hosts, containers and embedded vendor products; verify running versions after updates rather than relying on deployment tickets.
- **Management-plane hardening:** review Puppet certificate approval, segmentation and service-account privileges; document how to contain the control server without unnecessarily disrupting managed services.
- **Build-chain controls:** enforce trusted package sources, dependency pinning and provenance checks; reduce long-lived Azure/GitHub secrets on developer systems and ephemeral runners.
- **Web/mobile resilience:** review third-party script governance, payment-page integrity controls and managed iOS update compliance; request vendor incident scope and remediation evidence.
- **Backlog triage:** validate Oracle AutoVue/Agile and Wikimedia advisories against actual assets. Treat fresh exploit-index entries for older CVEs as renewed visibility—not proof of new vulnerabilities or active campaigns.
